hook_text: Four matchsticks, then seven, then ten. How many for picture 20? No drawing needed.
clip_script: One square: 4 matchsticks. Two squares side by side: 7, because they share a side. Three squares: 10. Each new square costs only 3 sticks: a top, a bottom and a right side. The left side is shared. So the rule is add 3. Picture 4: 13. Picture 5: 16. But what about picture 20? Look at the picture again. Twenty squares, 3 sticks each, is 60. Plus the one extra left side on the very first square. 61. The rule from the picture number: 3 times the number plus 1. Now a staircase of blocks: 1, 3, 6, 10. The jumps are 2, 3, 4. It grows by more each time, and that is still a pattern. See what changes, count it, say the rule, and the twentieth picture is yours without drawing a single square.
visual_style: Whiteboard matchstick squares appearing one by one with the 3 new sticks highlighted; a block staircase growing a column at a time; the number 61 appearing beside picture 20.
mood: Curious builder, satisfying leap to picture 20.
pacing: Three pictures built fast, the shared-side insight, the jump to picture 20, then the staircase contrast.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and build a matchstick pattern at home, then predict picture 10 before you build it.
